outcome: A refused candidate tells everyone why: seal and scope refusals persist the offending paths into the journal effect result and into the next try's worker context, so no worker ever retries blind against an invisible wall.

exclude: changing any error code already recorded in existing journals
changing what the seal or scope gates admit

acceptance.text: When sealTrackWithClaim or the refresh path refuses a candidate, the journal effect's result payload carries the refusal code and a bounded list of offending workspace-relative paths (first twenty plus a total count), proven by a test that seals a candidate with out-of-scope and reserved-root changes and reads the paths back from the journal.
ValidateSliceCandidateScope refusals carry the same bounded path evidence through the same channel, for both the out-of-scope and reserved-root cases.

A retry dispatch after a seal or scope refusal includes the prior refusal's code and paths in the worker's context, proven by a test that inspects the prepared dispatch inputs; a worker told which three paths fell outside scope can fix or drop them in one try.
Effects recorded by existing journals remain readable unchanged: the result payload is additive, no error code is renamed, and a regression test reads a pre-change journal fixture.

constraints: Refusal evidence is bounded and additive: journal schemas gain content inside the existing result payload, wire vocabulary is untouched, and nothing existing journals recorded becomes unreadable.
Evidence basis: run 2026-08-12-configurable-paths-r6 burned three ~600-turn tries against one invisible path family (sworn#203).
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
